tools: k-nearest neighbours: predict by the vote (or average) of the k closest training rows; knobs n_neighbors, weights, metric.
Small to medium data with a meaningful distance (after scaling); quick baselines; “show me similar cases”.
Just the neighbour search (no labels): kneighbors(X) returns distances and indices; brute force, KD-tree or ball tree.
Similarity search, deduplication, building features from neighbours.
Space-partitioning indexes for exact neighbour search; fast in low dimensions (below about 20).
Many queries on low-dimensional data; chosen automatically by algorithm="auto".
Exact and approximate nearest-neighbour indexes (IVF, product quantization, HNSW), CPU and GPU, up to billions of vectors.
Semantic search, retrieval for recommenders and RAG.
Approximate nearest neighbours with random-projection trees, stored as memory-mappable files.
Read-heavy similarity lookups such as music or item recommendations.
Naive Bayes for counts (word counts, TF-IDF): per-class word probabilities with smoothing alpha (default 1.0).
Text classification baselines, spam filtering; tiny data; streaming via partial_fit.
Naive Bayes that estimates each class from all the other classes' counts; corrects the skewed-data bias of MultinomialNB.
Text with imbalanced classes; often better than MultinomialNB on text.
Naive Bayes for binary features (word present / absent); absence is evidence too.
Naive Bayes for continuous features: a bell curve (mean, variance) per feature per class; no scaling needed.
Fast numeric baselines, streaming data; fails on strongly correlated features.
Kernel support vector classifier: C, kernel ("rbf" default, "poly", "linear", "sigmoid"), gamma (default "scale"). Outputs decision_function scores; probability=True is deprecated in 1.9.
Small to medium dense numeric data, curved boundaries; fit time at least quadratic in rows.
LinearSVC, Nystroem + linear model, gradient boosting
Linear SVM for large or sparse data; default loss is squared hinge, dual="auto".
Text classification, millions of rows, many features.
A linear SVM trained by stochastic gradient descent; supports partial_fit for data that doesn't fit in memory.
Huge or streaming data; after Nystroem or RBFSampler features.
Turns scores into calibrated probabilities with cross-validation: method="sigmoid" is Platt scaling; CalibratedClassifierCV(SVC(), ensemble=False) replaces SVC(probability=True).
Whenever you threshold or act on an SVM's or naive Bayes's probabilities.
Builds explicit features from a subsample of rows whose dot products approximate a kernel (n_components landmarks).
Kernel-like boundaries on data too big for SVC; follow with a linear model.
Random Fourier features (“random kitchen sinks”, Rahimi & Recht 2007) approximating the RBF kernel.
Very large data with an RBF-like boundary; streaming with SGD.
Compute kernel matrices K(X, Y) directly.
Checking the kernel trick, custom kernel methods, kernel="precomputed".
A kernel-based model whose predictions come with uncertainty; the kernel says how correlated two points' outputs are.
Small data where error bars matter; Bayesian optimization.
The solvers behind scikit-learn's SVC/SVR/OneClassSVM (LIBSVM) and LinearSVC/LogisticRegression(liblinear) (LIBLINEAR).
Directly from the command line or other languages; their practical guide is the SVM recipe.
acronyms: Predict from the k closest training points.
Find most of the true nearest neighbours much faster than an exact scan.
A graph index for ANN search: hop from neighbour to neighbour toward the query.
An ANN index that clusters vectors and only searches the nearest clusters.
Bayes' rule plus the assumption that features are independent given the class.
Naive Bayes estimated from the complement of each class; better on imbalanced text.
A max-margin classifier defined by its support vectors; with kernels it draws curved boundaries.
scikit-learn's names for kernel SVMs for classes and for numbers.
The algorithm that trains SVMs by updating two dual coefficients at a time (used by libsvm and this course's toy kit).
A kernel exp(−γ‖x − y‖²) that depends only on distance: similarity 1 at the same point, falling to 0 far away.
Random cosine features whose dot products approximate a shift-invariant kernel such as RBF.
terms: A model that stores the training data and does its work at prediction time, like kNN.
Neighbours vote with weight 1/d, so closer ones count more (weights="distance").
Straight-line distance; sum of absolute differences; 1 − cosine of the angle between vectors (good for text and embeddings).
In many dimensions space is so large that data is sparse, neighbourhoods stop being local and distances become nearly equal. Term coined by Richard Bellman.
As dimension grows, the nearest and farthest distances from a query become almost equal (ratio about 0.9 at d = 1,000 for uniform data).
The number of dimensions data really varies in (a surface inside a bigger space); kNN works when it's low.
P(class | evidence) ∝ P(evidence | class) × P(class): start from the base rate and update with the evidence.
How common each class is before looking at the features; in log-odds, the starting score.
Within each class, features are assumed unrelated, so the likelihood is a product of per-feature terms. Usually false; hurts probabilities more than rankings.
Add α pretend counts to every word in every class (α = 1 Laplace, α < 1 Lidstone) so no probability is 0.
log P(word | spam) − log P(word | ham): how much one occurrence pushes the log-odds toward spam.
Predicted probabilities more extreme than reality (says 97%, right 78%); typical of naive Bayes. Fix with calibration.
naive Bayes, boosted trees, neural nets
The empty band around an SVM's boundary between scores −1 and +1; its width is 2/‖w‖.
The training points on or inside the margin; the SVM's solution is a weighted sum of them only.
Hard: no point may enter the street (separable data only). Soft: points may, at a cost C × their violation.
Price of margin violations. Small C: wide street, more support vectors, more regularization. Large C: narrow street, fits training points closely.
max(0, 1 − y·f(x)): zero beyond the margin, linear inside it. Squared hinge is its square (LinearSVC's default).
One weight per training point in the SVM's dual problem; non-zero only for support vectors.
Fit a sigmoid that maps classifier scores to probabilities on held-out data.
A function K(x, y) equal to a dot product of (possibly huge) feature maps φ(x)·φ(y): a similarity measure.
Run a method that only needs dot products (SVM, ridge, PCA) with K(x, y) in their place, working in the lifted space without building it. Example: (x·y)² = degree-2 features' dot product.
The transformation into new features where the classes become linearly separable, e.g. z = x² + y² for rings.
(γ·x·y + r)^p: all products of features up to degree p.
Width knob of the RBF kernel: each support vector reaches about 1/√γ. Small γ smooth, large γ memorizes. Default "scale" = 1 / (n_features × variance of X).
The n × n table of kernel values between training points; why kernel methods cost O(n²) memory and at least O(n²) time.
Explicit features (Nystroem landmarks or random Fourier features) whose dot products approximate a kernel, so a fast linear model can be used.
